summary: Deployed inventory-worker as a hardened systemd service on node1: runs as dedicated unprivileged system user inventory-worker, loops writing a counter and log line every 10s, confined to /var/lib/inventory via ProtectSystem=strict + ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory + ProtectHome, with NoNewPrivileges=yes and a broad set of additional systemd sandboxing directives (PrivateTmp, PrivateDevices, RestrictNamespaces, MemoryDenyWriteExecute, CapabilityBoundingSet=, etc). Verified confinement by falsification (same-profile write to /var/lib/inventory succeeds; writes to /root and /etc fail). Completed mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured pre-reboot boot_id and service/data state, issued systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified the service re-enabled/re-started automatically with data (count, log) intact and continuing to grow.
actions_performed: Created system user inventory-worker with nologin shell, no home dir creation
Wrote worker script /usr/local/lib/inventory-worker/worker.sh (loop writing count+log to /var/lib/inventory every 10s)

Created /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service with NoNewPrivileges=yes, ProtectSystem=strict, ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory, ProtectHome, PrivateTmp/Devices, RestrictNamespaces, MemoryDenyWriteExecute, CapabilityBoundingSet=, SystemCallFilter=@system-service, etc.
Ran systemd-analyze verify on the unit (clean)
systemctl daemon-reload; enable --now inventory-worker.service; confirmed active/running with correct uid=999 and NoNewPrivs=1
Falsification test via systemd-run with same security properties: write to /var/lib/inventory succeeds, /root permission denied, /etc read-only filesystem
Captured baseline boot_id and service/data state pre-restart
Issued backgrounded systemctl reboot so acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again
Verified inventory-worker.service enabled+active post-reboot and count/log continued from prior persisted state

evidence.requirement: Service installed and running, confined to /var/lib/inventory, NoNewPrivileges
evidence.summary: Unit created, verified clean by systemd-analyze, started successfully; runtime proc status shows uid=999 (unprivileged) and NoNewPrivs=1; data files written only under /var/lib/inventory
Same-profile process: write to /var/lib/inventory succeeds (exit 0), write to /root denied (Permission denied), write to /etc denied (Read-only file system)
Captured boot_id 96c08b66-5aa4-4e9a-b76f-04e2c6e34ced, service enabled+active, count=3, log entries present
Backgrounded systemctl reboot command returned 'reboot_issued' before node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving actual restart
evidence.summary: Node unreachable during reboot (connection reset/timeout), then reachable again with new boot_id 9939bbff-1f14-4e1f-b25c-f0b5ea9b2cbc, differing from pre-restart baseline

inventory-worker.service enabled and active (auto-started post-boot), count advanced 3->4, worker.log preserved and appended, confirming both service persistence and data durability in /var/lib/inventory across restart
